title: FlowCast: Advancing Precipitation Nowcasting with Conditional Flow Matching
claim: A latent encoder feeds a U-Net-style stack of time-conditioned convolution and attention blocks that predicts a vector field, shown with block-level detail.
layout: Main vertical stack on the left, input at top and output at bottom, with a skip connection. Two zoomed-in block diagrams on the right, with shapes labeled underneath.
description: A detailed architecture diagram. At top left, stacked radar frames (input) pass through a green trapezoid encoder labeled E, producing a blue latent volume. Beside it sits a noisy latent, with the interpolation formula Z_t = (1-t)Z_P + tZ_future above it. Both feed down into a vertical stack of white boxes: Observation Masking, Conv Block, 4x Time Conv + Cuboid Attn, Downsample, 4x Time Conv + Cuboid Attn, Upsample, 4x Time Conv + Cuboid Attn, Linear Layer. A dashed brown skip arrow links the first and last attention blocks. The output is a noisy-looking latent labeled v_theta. At right, two outlined boxes expand the Conv Block (GroupNorm, SiLU, Conv3D repeated) and the Time Conv Block, which adds a t~U(0,1) branch through SiLU and Linear into a summation node. Border colors mark the module types. Tensor shapes are written under the arrows.
caption: The FlowCast architecture. A U-Net with Cuboid Attention blocks processes latent spatiotemporal data. Conditioning on the flow time t enables the model to learn the time-dependent vector field for generating forecasts.
abstract: Radar-based precipitation nowcasting, the task of forecasting short-term precipitation fields from previous radar images, is a critical problem for flood risk management and decision-making. While deep learning has substantially advanced this field, two challenges remain fundamental: the uncertainty of atmospheric dynamics and the efficient modeling of high-dimensional data. Diffusion models have shown strong promise by producing sharp, reliable forecasts, but their iterative sampling process is computationally prohibitive for time-critical applications. We introduce FlowCast, the first end-to-end probabilistic model leveraging Conditional Flow Matching (CFM) as a direct noise-to-data generative framework for precipitation nowcasting. Unlike hybrid approaches, FlowCast learns a direct noise-to-data mapping in a compressed latent space, enabling rapid, high-fidelity sample generation. Our experiments demonstrate that FlowCast establishes a new state-of-the-art in probabilistic performance while also exceeding deterministic baselines in predictive accuracy. A direct comparison further reveals the CFM objective is both more accurate and significantly more efficient than a diffusion objective on the same architecture, maintaining high performance with significantly fewer sampling steps. This work positions CFM as a powerful and practical alternative for high-dimensional spatiotemporal forecasting.
